To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stimulation of renal afferent nerves causes an increase in the sympathetic tone and that this increase in the sympathetic activity is mediated by the central nervous system.

stimulation of a renal afferent nerve bundle results in increased sympathetic tone, increased systemic blood pressure, increased efferent activity of the renal sympathetic nerves, and a reduction in the blood flow to the kidneys, and this response can be recorded in both kidneys, even if only one of them is stimulated.

stimulation of the intact renal nerves at a frequency of five Hz resulted in a 15% fall of the total and regional renal perfusion in both the ipsilateral and the contralateral kidneys, but that this response was lost if the nerves were cut before the stimulation electrodes or after them, meaning that only the afferent renal nerve fibres were stimulated.

the reno-renal (renal-renal) reflex.
the evaluation of the renal sympathetic nerves, and the role played by the renal receptors in the regulation of renal blood flow and systemic blood pressure.
the reno-renal (renal-renal) reflex, which is a reflex arc involving the kidney, the renal nerves, the central nervous system and the kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reno-renal and renorenal reflexes are mediated via afferent and efferent renal nerves.
the renal nerves are involved in a reno-renal feedback loop, and that the afferent renal nerves are responsible for the initiation and control of the reflex.
afferent renal nerve fibres have an important influence on the general sympathetic tone and the blood pressure level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reno-renal and renal-renal reflexes exist, but that the afferent renal nerves are not necessary for the reno- renal reflex to be established.
the reno-renal and the renal-renal reflexes exist, but the reno-reno-reflex is of minor importance.

the renal nerves are not only involved in the control of the blood flow to the kidneys, but also play a major role in the control of systemic blood pressure and in the control of blood flow to other organs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

renal afferent nerves are important for the regulation of systemic blood pressure and that the reno-renal afferent nerves have the potential to influence the sympathetic tone in a way that is independent of the baroreflex.
the kidneys are not only organs that respond to the central nervous system, but also that they can affect it.
renal afferents are important to maintain the systemic blood pressure.
